transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-01
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Celestia Head of Data Governance), Ethan (Celestia Lead SRE), Liam (Celestia Compliance Counsel)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: quick intake on key residency needs and log sanitization; clarified that Celestia is leaning Private for PHI work but wants cost/latency comparison for predictive models.
Topics: KMS residency, audit evidence, log redaction, hosting choice.
Action items (see metadata).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. quick round of intros and then we can jump into the residency and keystore questions.
[00:08] Priya: Hi, Priya here. Head of data governance at Celestia. we own policy and the compliance gating.
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan, I run platform/SRE. I'll be focused on operations and throughput.
[00:17] Liam: Liam, legal and compliance. mostly here for scope and evidence needs.
[00:21] Diego: Diego from Redwood, I'm the systems SE, happy to go deep on KMS and logs.
[00:28] Maya: Great. high level — remind me, Priya, what's the primary workload? is it customer PII/PHI or aggregated market analytics?
[00:36] Priya: It's a mix. our pricing models and some risk models handle customer financial data, and a subset of research has PHI-like health flags. So GDPR applies and also HIPAA for certain pipelines. We need to be strict about residency and key control.
[00:49] Maya: Understood. so the choice between Hosted, Dedicated, Private — typical tradeoffs. hosted gives fastest time-to-prototype, dedicated gives reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem) gives you the strongest isolation for residency and key management.
[01:03] Priya: Yep. A few specific asks up front: 1) We cannot have customer data or audit logs egress the EU for EU-subject data. 2) Keys for decrypting any PI must be under our control and rotatable on our schedule. 3) Logs must be redacted before retention; and we need immutable audit trails for legal hold.
[01:24] Diego: Quick clarification — when you say "keys under your control" do you mean customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) with HSM-backed keys, or are you open to Redwood-managed keys with strict SLAs and proof of residency?
[01:36] Priya: Prefer BYOK with HSM. internal policy says keys must not be exportable off the EU tenancy, and we want to review key rotation policies before go-live.
[01:48] Liam: Also, on legal hold: we may need to preserve raw inputs for investigations for up to 7 years; must be able to freeze or hand over evidence with chain-of-custody metadata. so logs can't be trimmed in a way that loses evidentiary context.
[02:03] Maya: Okay good, that's clear. Diego, can you talk through KMS options? region pinning? we have a Private product with on-prem option and a VPC flow for EU-only control.
[02:12] Diego: Sure. two main patterns we typically present: 1) Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC or on-prem appliance — here the customer retains their KMS entirely; Redwood's control plane can be run in a region of your choosing but the inference plane and all logs stay inside the tenancy. 2) Dedicated in Redwood cloud — we can support BYOK where you supply keys via a customer KMS, but you need a key wrapping/rotation agreement; some customers are comfortable with that for EU-only deployments but it requires our cross-account roles to be strictly scoped.
[02:41] Ethan: For Dedicated with BYOK, how do you prevent debug traces or KV cache snapshots making it back to Redwood logs in a way we can't control?
[02:50] Diego: Good callout. we have automatic redaction hooks and a KV cache scrubber. but transcription note: the automated scrub is not perfect — we recommend a two-stage approach: first, enforce strict request-level redaction rules (client-side filtering, prompt templates), second, configure Redwood runtimes to drop selected trace-level logs and keep only abstract metrics. for forensic needs we can enable a secure evidence channel where raw inputs are placed into your S3 under your encryption.
[03:17] Priya: That 'evidence channel' sounds promising. does it respect legal hold? we need an append-only store with retention flags controlled by us, and log integrity checks.
[03:26] Diego: Yes — we can write raw artifacts to a customer-owned bucket/Blob with server-side encryption using your keys. retention and immutability are controlled by your bucket's policies (WORM style). Redwood's audit log will still show an event pointer but will not contain the raw PII.
[03:39] Liam: What's the chain-of-custody metadata you can provide? timestamps, operator IDs, commits, model versions?
[03:46] Diego: We capture request id, model id and model hash, sequence of fallbacks, worker node id (or obfuscated id if in hosted), and an action audit with timestamps and the route used. If you need more, we can extend to include the signed attestations from the inference node.
[03:58] Priya: For GDPR we also need proof that no replica of logs was stored outside EU. how do you prove that?
[04:06] Diego: For Private deployments it's straightforward — everything lives in your VPC/region. For Dedicated we can provide region-locked capacity and signed attestations, plus access to our infra audit logs that show network egress denied. It isn't the same as giving you physical access but it's typical enterprise evidence.
[04:21] Maya: Another real-world constraint — latency. Ethan, what are your SLOs for the pricing models?
[04:25] Ethan: P99 under 250ms for short prompts, throughput around 25 tokens/sec sustained per user batch. If Dedicated or Private increases latency beyond 20% it's a problem for product.
[04:36] Diego: Performance note — Private on-prem can actually be lower latency if you colocate GPUs near your services; the tradeoff is ops overhead. Dedicated has predictable throughput but slightly higher tail latency depending on region routing and multi-tenant noise.
[04:51] Priya: Cost is also a factor. Legal is pushing Private for PHI but business wants Hosted for experimentation. Is there a hybrid — flow that splits PHI to Private and pseudonymized prompts to Hosted?
[05:02] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing policies — you can route by data classification at the API layer. we can set routing rules to send PHI to your Private cluster, and aggregated analytics to Hosted.
[05:12] Liam: On auditability: we need to know who accessed keys, when, and whether Redwood personnel had any admin access. how does Redwood's SRE access look in Private mode?
[05:22] Diego: In Private, you control the tenancy and keys; Redwood support access can be configured via just-in-time temporary roles and recorded sessions. we also support staff access via SAML-backed bastion and session recordings.
[05:33] Priya: A small nit — retention of the token-level cost data. Finance wants token-level billing but we can't have the raw prompts leak. so we need aggregated billing with token counts but not content.
[05:45] Maya: That's normal. we provide token usage metrics and cost breakdowns without storing prompt text; you can map usage to tenant ids.
[05:51] Ethan: A technical question — you mentioned KV cache scrubbing earlier. does that mean the KV stays local and never persisted? and can we set TTLs?
[05:58] Diego: KV is in-memory by default; for very large context we may write checkpointed state to local disk, but for Private we can disable persistence. TTLs and eviction policies are configurable. note: sometimes the transcript generator mislabels "KV cache" as "K V cash" in our older logs, but it's the same.
[06:17] Priya: Good to know. Can you summarize evidence we can expect for SOC2 or HIPAA audits?
[06:24] Diego: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagrams showing network flows, KMS integration docs, retention policy configs, and signed attestations for region-locking. If needed, Redwood's security team can do a joint webinar with your auditors.
[06:38] Liam: will you give us a written playbook for legal hold extraction? we want step-by-step instructions, estimated time to retrieve artifacts, and a sample chain-of-custody export.
[06:48] Maya: absolutely — Diego, we'll draft that playbook and include estimated RTO/RPO for evidence requests.
[06:55] Diego: I'll take that action. also, for the pilot we typically propose 2-3 week Dedicated trial with sample models and an EU-only region. we'll capture perf and costs so you can compare to Hosted and Private.
[07:07] Ethan: that's useful. one more ops detail — do you support customer-managed VPC endpoints so that egress is entirely through our firewall?
[07:14] Diego: Yes, for VPC deployments we support interface endpoints and private link equivalents. For Dedicated we can set up a peered VPC or private link depending on cloud.
[07:25] Priya: ok next steps for us: legal will review the SOC2 and KMS docs; engineering will schedule the SE deep dive; and procurement will want a pilot pricing note.
[07:36] Maya: Great — recap: Redwood will send SOC2 + KMS integration + network diagram (Maya), SE will prepare pilot checklist and perf numbers (Diego), Celestia will share KMS provider details and compliance matrix (Ethan), and legal will propose the legal-hold playbook items to be discussed Oct 8 (Liam).
[07:57] Liam: sounds right. small aside — competitor mention: we've had chats with Anthropic and tried an in-house smoke test. their response times were okay but they lacked the BYOK workarounds we need.
[08:09] Maya: Helpful context. Any other questions?
[08:12] Priya: Not right now. we will review docs and come back with redlines.
[08:16] Ethan: we'll aim to have the KMS provider doc by Oct 7.
[08:19] Maya: Perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and legal session.
[08:25] [Crosstalk] brief goodbyes and meeting end.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard technical terms ("K V cash" instead of KV cache), some timestamps approximate. There are places where speaker attribution might be imperfect (e.g., short interjections).
